To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dosimetric chain of molecular radiotherapy can be extended into the cell level, and that the dose distribution in 3D cell aggregates can be simulated with the Monte Carlo code Geant4-DNA.
a multicellular dosimetric model can be used to predict cell survival after irradiation of multicellular structures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a multicellular dosimetric (MCD) model for molecular radiotherapy.
developing an accurate, efficient and reliable method to simulate the dose distribution in a 3D spheroid.
the development and application of a new approach for the dosimetric characterization of the molecular radiotherapy of tumors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dosimetric chain of molecular radiotherapy has to be adapted to multicellular systems.
the dose-response curves of cells exposed to radiation in the low dose range are non-linear, and are not well described by linear-quadratic models.
the dose to a cell nucleus is the sum of the contributions of all radiation components, and that the dose to the cell nucleus is the most important parameter for cell survival.

we have developed a novel dosimetric framework that can be applied for molecular radiotherapy.

the dosimetric chain in molecular radiotherapy is a complex multicellular process.
